rows.subtype: Approach: reading signals and accepting a no [Thinking]
rows.description: The student decides in advance that a hesitant or clear refusal will be taken at face value, with no pushing, repeated messages or asking friends to pressure. Respect matters more than the outcome.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, mental simulation, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.description: Inspired by films, a student plans to ask in front of the whole class with flowers. The audience pressure makes a comfortable answer difficult and can embarrass the other person, whatever the reply.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, mental simulation, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: never acting due to fear of rejection [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student rehearses endlessly and never speaks, and after months the crush starts talking with someone else. Avoidance protects from a no but also removes any chance of a yes.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.description: The student asks in person, quietly, after a club meeting, or by a short private message, saying she likes talking with him and asking if he would like to get chai together some time.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, mental simulation, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: considering family rules and school norms [Thinking]
rows.description: The student thinks about the family's expectations and school rules, and chooses a group setting during daytime, thinking about safety, honesty with parents where possible, and comfort for both people.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, mental simulation, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: relying on friends as messengers [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student asks a friend to find out if the crush likes him. The message gets distorted, becomes gossip, and the other person feels talked about instead of asked directly.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, mental simulation, trial by imitation

rows.subtype: Approach: handling a rejection and recovering [Revision]
rows.description: After a polite no, the student thanks her, gives space, spends time with friends and sport, and notes that disappointment fades. Continuing normal friendly behaviour keeps the classroom comfortable.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, mental simulation, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.description: Noticing that thoughts about the crush are crowding out study, the student limits social media checking, tells a trusted friend, and puts the energy into a project, which reduces the intensity.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: mental simulation, seeking advice, trial by imitation

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: deciding values and limits in advance [Thinking]
rows.description: Before a party, the student decides what he will not do, such as riding with an unsafe driver or trying substances, so that decisions in the moment follow a rule already thought through.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, prioritising

rows.subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
rows.subtype: Approach: prepared refusal lines and exit plan [Action]
rows.description: The student prepares a short refusal, such as no thanks, I am good, and agrees with a parent on a code word to be picked up, so leaving does not require an argument or explanation.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, inversion, prioritising, values-first planning
